title: Customer Reactivation Campaign Strategies That Gets Lost Customers Back

facts.fact: Reactivating a lapsed customer costs 5–7x less than acquiring an equivalent new customer, per the vendor's blog.
facts.quote: Reactivating a lapsed customer costs 5–7x less than acquiring an equivalent new customer

facts.fact: The page states that the benchmark reactivation rate for B2B reactivation campaigns is 5–15%.
facts.quote: Reactivation rate: benchmark for B2B reactivation campaigns is 5–15%

facts.fact: For SaaS businesses, the page suggests an inactivity threshold of 30 days without login.
facts.quote: SaaS: 30 days without login

facts.fact: For B2B services, the page suggests an inactivity threshold of 90 days without a touchpoint or purchase.
facts.quote: B2B services: 90 days without a touchpoint or purchase

facts.fact: For ecommerce, the page suggests an inactivity threshold of 60–90 days without an order.
facts.quote: Ecommerce: 60–90 days without an order

facts.fact: The page recommends a 4–5 touch multi-channel reactivation sequence rather than a one-time blast.
facts.quote: Build a 4–5 touch sequence, not a one-time blast

facts.fact: The page recommends spacing reactivation touches 5–7 days apart.
facts.quote: Space touches 5–7 days apart.

facts.fact: The page recommends starting the reactivation sequence at the 30–60 day dormancy mark.
facts.quote: Starting the sequence at the 30–60 day dormancy mark gives you the best shot at reactivation

facts.fact: In the page's sample five-touch sequence, Touch 1 is a soft check-in on Day 1, with no pitch.
facts.quote: Touch 1 | Day 1 | Soft check-in — what's changed, no pitch

facts.fact: In the page's sample five-touch sequence, the incentive offer is Touch 4 on Day 21.
facts.quote: Touch 4 | Day 21 | Incentive offer — time-limited, segment-appropriate

facts.fact: The page recommends tracking 90-day retention rate after reactivation as the real north star metric.
facts.quote: 90-day retention rate post-reactivation (this is your real north star)

facts.fact: The page suggests reviewing NPS trends in the 60 days before disengagement when diagnosing churn.
facts.quote: Look at exit notes, NPS trends in the 60 days before disengagement

facts.fact: The page's tiering model assigns Tier 3 (low LTV, dormant 12+ months) to light-touch email only or suppression.
facts.quote: Tier 3 | Low LTV, dormant 12+ months | Light-touch email only or suppression

facts.fact: Global email open rate benchmark for reactivation campaigns reached an average of 21.4% in 2025, according to a third-party source (growthwayadvertising.com), up from 17% in 2023.
facts.quote: Global email open rate benchmarks for [reactivation campaigns climbed to an average of 21.4%](https://growthwayadvertising.com/the-best-re-engagement-email-templates-backed-by-open-rate-data/) in 2025, up from 17% in 2023

facts.fact: The 2023 baseline for the average global email open rate for reactivation campaigns was 17%, per the same third-party source cited by the page.
facts.quote: up from 17% in 2023

facts.fact: The page states that roughly 45% of customers who receive a reactivation email open subsequent emails; no source is given for this vendor-stated benchmark.
facts.quote: **Reactivation email benchmark:** Roughly 45% of customers who receive a reactivation email open subsequent emails

facts.fact: The page recommends A/B testing subject lines with at least 200 contacts per variant before scaling a reactivation email.
facts.quote: A/B test subject lines with at least 200 contacts per variant before scaling

facts.fact: The page recommends that the offer appear only in touches 3–4 of an email reactivation sequence.
facts.quote: **Offer (touches 3–4 only):** Specific, time-bound, and segment-appropriate

facts.fact: The page recommends keeping SMS or push notification messages under 160 characters for reactivation.
facts.quote: Keep messages under 160 characters and lead with value

facts.fact: The page recommends that an SDR's reactivation call to a former customer be kept under three minutes.
facts.quote: Keep it under three minutes. Don't pitch. Qualify.

facts.fact: In the B2B 'We Miss You' sequence example, the 20% discount or free onboarding offer is sent on Day 14, after case-study and value-reframe touches.
facts.quote: | Day 14 | 20% discount or free onboarding + specific deadline |

facts.fact: In the B2B 'We Miss You' sequence example, touches are scheduled on Days 1, 7, 14, and 21.
facts.quote: | Day 1 | "It's been [X months] — wanted to check in" (no offer) |

facts.fact: In the LinkedIn plus email coordinated example for Tier 1 accounts, the sequence runs over 14 days with touches on Days 1, 3, 7, and 14.
facts.quote: | Day 14 | Email with offer + retargeting ad running in background |

facts.fact: Brex used AI-powered signals to identify lapsed customers, and the page reports this produced a 40% increase in booked demos from formerly dormant accounts.
facts.quote: The result was a 40% increase in booked demos from formerly dormant accounts.

facts.fact: Database reactivation campaigns recover 5–15% of dormant leads on average, per a third-party source cited by the page.
facts.quote: Database reactivation campaigns recover 5–15% of dormant leads on average — this is your benchmark range for B2B

facts.fact: The page gives a healthy email open rate benchmark for reactivation campaigns of 12–15%, and says below 8% signals a subject line or list quality problem.
facts.quote: Open rate: 12–15% is healthy for reactivation; below 8% signals a subject line or list quality problem

facts.fact: The page gives a click-through rate benchmark of 2–5% for reactivation emails.
facts.quote: Click-through rate: 2–5% benchmark

facts.fact: The page states an unsubscribe rate above 0.5% means the message-to-list match is off.
facts.quote: Unsubscribe rate: above 0.5% means your message-to-list match is off

facts.fact: For high LTV accounts the page recommends a 25–30% discount or VIP offer plus concierge onboarding as incentive.
facts.quote: High LTV accounts | 25–30% discount or VIP offer + concierge onboarding

facts.fact: For mid LTV accounts the page recommends a 10–15% discount or extended trial as incentive.
facts.quote: Mid LTV accounts | 10–15% discount or extended trial

facts.fact: The page recommends escalating to an incentive only on touches 3–4, after leading with value on touches 1–2.
facts.quote: Start with value and "what's new" on touches 1–2. Escalate to an incentive only on touches 3–4.

facts.fact: The page says if reactivated customers churn again within 60 days, the campaign did not fix the underlying problem.
facts.quote: if reactivated customers are churning again within 60 days, the campaign didn't fix the underlying problem.

facts.fact: The page recommends running cohort analysis comparing LTV of reactivated customers against continuously active customers over 6–12 months.
facts.quote: Compare the LTV of reactivated customers against continuously active customers tracked over 6–12 months.

facts.fact: The page lists declining email open rates over 4+ consecutive weeks as an early warning signal of at-risk accounts.
facts.quote: Declining email open rates over 4+ consecutive weeks.

facts.fact: Cleverly states it has generated over $312M in pipeline for clients through outbound programs.
facts.quote: We've generated over $312M in pipeline for clients through outbound programs

facts.fact: Cleverly states it is trusted by 10,000+ clients.
facts.quote: trusted by 10,000+ clients

facts.fact: Cleverly's LinkedIn services start at $397 per month, according to the page.
facts.quote: [LinkedIn services](https://www.cleverly.co/linkedin-lead-generation) start at $397/month

facts.fact: Cleverly states its cold email model means clients only pay for meeting-ready leads delivered.
facts.quote: our [cold email model](https://www.cleverly.co/cold-email-outreach-agency) means you only pay for meeting-ready leads we deliver.

facts.fact: The page recommends running a 4–5 touch reactivation sequence across email and LinkedIn for dormant accounts.
facts.quote: run a 4–5 touch sequence across email and LinkedIn, leading with what's changed or improved since they left

facts.fact: The page states a benchmark reactivation rate of 5–15% for B2B campaigns.
facts.quote: reactivation rate (benchmark: 5–15% for B2B)

facts.fact: The page states that 90-day retention rate post-reactivation is the most important metric for reactivation campaigns.
facts.quote: The 90-day retention rate is the most important — if reactivated customers are churning again within two months

facts.fact: The page recommends reserving incentives for later touches in a reactivation sequence rather than leading with them.
facts.quote: Reserve incentives for later touches, and bring in SDR outreach for high-value accounts.

facts.fact: The page identifies email as the primary channel for most reactivation programs.
facts.quote: Email is the primary channel for most reactivation programs due to its scalability and personalizability.

facts.fact: The page describes LinkedIn Sales Navigator outreach and sponsored InMail as the highest-leverage second channel for B2B reactivation.
facts.quote: LinkedIn is the highest-leverage second channel for B2B, particularly through Sales Navigator outreach and sponsored InMail.

facts.fact: The page recommends tracking four core reactivation metrics: reactivation rate, revenue per reactivated customer, campaign ROI, and 90-day retention rate.
facts.quote: Track four core metrics: reactivation rate (benchmark: 5–15% for B2B), revenue per reactivated customer, campaign ROI, and 90-day retention rate post-reactivation.
